answer: Each agent can submit only one claim per epoch, and a randomly selected sample of its transactions must be backed by a refundable stake locked until independent reviewers verify them. A false or duplicated identity risks forfeiting that stake, while splitting into many identities multiplies the capital required to influence the sample. The check should compare signed transaction histories, not names: quartz recorded at dawn may trace through a canyon of accounts, but the attacker still has to fund every exposed claim.
